source_evidence.location: PDF page 6, printed page 10, Bernoulli-sums paragraph immediately before Equation (1.7)
source_evidence.anchor: The sum S_N := X_1 + ··· + X_N is said to have the binomial distribution Binom(N,p).
source_evidence.observation: For iid Bernoulli random variables X_i with fixed parameter p in (0,1), their sum through a positive integer N has binomial distribution Binom(N,p).

hypotheses: X_1, ..., X_N are independent and identically distributed
For each i with 1 ≤ i ≤ N, X_i ∼ Ber(p)
definitions_and_conventions: X_i ∼ Ber(p) means that X_i takes the values 1 and 0 with probabilities p and 1-p, respectively
implicit_context: The random variables are defined in a common probabilistic setting so that their sum is meaningful.
The parameter p is fixed across the iid Bernoulli variables.

semantic_facets.topic: binomial law of a Bernoulli sum
details: A finite sum of N iid Bernoulli(p) random variables is distributed as Binom(N,p).

undebatable_constraints: The summands must be iid Bernoulli random variables with the same fixed parameter p.
The number of summands N must be a positive integer.
The summed random variable must be S_N := X_1 + ··· + X_N.
The conclusion is the distributional assertion S_N ∼ Binom(N,p).
The separate displayed central-limit formula labeled Equation (1.7) is not part of this contract.
contract_plain_english: Given a positive integer N and iid Bernoulli(p) random variables X_1 through X_N for a fixed p strictly between 0 and 1, define S_N as their sum. Then S_N has the binomial distribution with parameters N and p.
